newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico minister says petrochemical sale on track.
newsitem.headline: Mexico minister says petrochemical sale on track.

text.p: Mexican Energy Minister Jesus Reyes Heroles on Thursday said the partial privatization of the country's petrochemical sector was on track, though the government still could not offer specifics on how the sale would proceed.

"At this moment nothing is decided. It is all still being studied and will not be completed until August, when we have a concrete scheme with all details defined," Reyes told reporters during a natural gas industry conference in Cancun.

He reiterated that the government intended to announce how it would sell a minority stake in the nation's 12 state-owned petrochemical plants. He said the government has held talks with private investors and clients regarding the planned sale.
An expected invitation to bidding companies in the second half of the year would follow years of delays and confusion over the future of the sector.

Eight of the petrochemcial complexes have already been disincorporated from state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), and Reyes said in the next two months the remaining four will be separated.
